title: BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) - WiFi 2.4 GHz for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Mei-Ling Chen

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) filter targeting WiFi 2.4 GHz for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on PZT on Si substrate with a target center frequency of 5197.1 MHz and bandwidth of 323.3 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave)
- Frequency Band: WiFi 2.4 GHz
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: PZT on Si
- Package: SiP (System in Package)
- Design Tool: Keysight ADS 2024
- Design Center: Helsinki 5G Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) design targeting WiFi 2.4 GHz. Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       5197.1 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       323.3 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.9 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 8.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 28.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 30.0 dB
Q Factor:               4669
Temperature Coefficient:-21.7 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.7 x 1.0 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   9
Electrode Material:     W
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Keysight ADS 2024 and load the BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: PZT on Si with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 5197.1 MHz, BW 323.3 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.9 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (SiP (System in Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, PZT on Si).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N9041B UXA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 15591 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.9 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 8.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 485 MHz offset >= 28.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 7 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 14.1 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +25 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 89%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-06-12
Devices Tested:         14
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.57 dB
Return Loss (meas):     10.0 dB
Rejection (meas):       30.5 dB
Isolation (meas):       35.2 dB
Q Factor (meas):        4669
Group Delay Variation:  1.4 ns
Power Handling:         +36 dBm
Die Yield:              97.8%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) design demonstrated below-target performance for WiFi 2.4 GHz.
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Simulation-to-measurement correlation was within 3% for all key parameters.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
